newsitem.title: USA: Edison offers new Calif. nuke marine plan.
newsitem.headline: Edison offers new Calif. nuke marine plan.

text.p: Edison International's Southern California Edison Co proposed Wednesday "a significant compromise" on marine environmental concerns linked to its San Onofre nuclear power plant at San Clemente, Calif.
Edison outlined its proposal in a letter to the California Coastal Commission, which is set to hold a public hearing on the issue next Wednesday in San Diego.

Edison, the majority owner and operator of the nuclear plant, has sought to revise a 1991 agreement to construct a 300-acre artificial kelp reef, which it now says is not justified by scientific evidence.

Among the key elements of Edison's proposal is an option for the company to establish a $28-million mitigation fund for the Coastal Conservancy to build a wetland restoration project in San Diego County.
Edison would set aside another $3 million for a wetland restoration project in Ventura County.
The proposal also would expand Edison's plan to fund construction of a 16.8-acre experimental kelp reef as well as a study to determine the viability of artificial reefs.
Should the reef experiment succeed at the end of a 10-year period, Edison would extend the reef to a total 56.3 acres or provide funding for its extension.

If, however, artificial kelp reefs are found not to be viable after the 10-year experiment, Edison would agree to pay $3.5 million, plus interest accrued over the 10-year study period, to implement alternative marine conservation and enhancement projects designated by the Commission.
Edison also seeks new options for monitoring mitigation activities.
Also, the utility said it would establish a $5-million interest-bearing remediation fund to be used for restoration and enhancement of wetlands or other marine resources.
